baseline_models.focus_anchor: The calling verb at word 2 takes the ruin noun at word 3, allowing the utterance both to name perdition and to try to draw it near.
baseline_models.mechanism: A vocal act reaches toward its own catastrophic object. Ruin is therefore not only reported as an emotion; it is invoked as the desired event.

activation_trace.role: Calling that draws something near by speech makes the verb an attempted performative rather than bare noise.
Ruin, loss, and corruption supply the catastrophic object the call tries to actualize.

changed_reading.before: He will cry out because he is ruined.
changed_reading.after: He will use the cry itself to summon ruin toward himself.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ruin noun at word 3 also carries restraint, prevention, and being turned away, while word 2 is an explicit call.
baseline_models.mechanism: The requested object can be cessation rather than simple annihilation: stop this, hold it back, or remove me from its reach. The line becomes a plea for an arresting boundary.

activation_trace.role: The vocal drawing-near branch frames the clause as a directed request.
Blocking, restraining, and turning away recast the requested ruin as a demand for cessation or removal.

changed_reading.after: He asks for an intervention that will stop, block, or turn away what has begun.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The calling root at word 2 contains an image of one part falling after another, directly beside the perdition noun at word 3.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verb imports a sequential-collapse image into the utterance. The speaker is not only naming a terminal state; his call sounds like the first falling part of a ruin that propagates through the rest.

activation_trace.role: Successive falling gives the act of calling a cascading material profile and makes the cry the first link in collapse.
Perdition supplies the terminal condition toward which the cascade runs.

changed_reading.before: The cry follows an already completed disaster.
changed_reading.after: The cry can be heard as one event in a ruin that falls forward part by part.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same noun at word 3 carries both ruin and steady persistence, producing a live internal tension in what is called for.
baseline_models.mechanism: Perdition becomes the name shouted when continuation is itself unbearable. The speaker asks for an end, but the selected word also carries the very persistence from which he seeks release.

activation_trace.role: Ruin supplies the desired terminal pole of the cry.
Steady persistence places unwanted continuance inside the very word used to demand an end.
Directed calling turns the lexical tension into an urgent request.

changed_reading.before: Perdition is a single terminal event.
changed_reading.after: Perdition is the paradoxical name for the end desired from a condition that keeps persisting.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening sequence splits a boundary, stretches a surface, casts out contents, and leaves the container empty. The focus roots' collapse and opening branches compress that material sequence into a human utterance, so the called-for ruin can mean being unsealed and emptied rather than merely killed.

activation_trace.role: Successive collapse lets the human call echo the ordered breakdown of the surrounding world.
Receding and opening turn perdition into an unsealing process.
Splitting and opening provide the first material operation that the focus cry miniaturizes.
Drawing a thing out lengthwise supplies the exposed, extended surface on which emptying occurs.
Casting until a thing lies outside supplies the expulsion phase of the mechanism.
A place stripped and left vacant supplies the endpoint of complete emptying.

structural_cues: 84:1-4 form an ordered split, stretch, cast, and empty sequence before the human record scene.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the material sequence and focus branches for collapse and opening; I infer a macrocosm-to-person echo. A live alternative is that the cosmic sequence only establishes setting and the cry remains ordinary lament.

changed_reading.before: He generically calls for death amid a collapsing cosmos.
changed_reading.after: He calls to be opened, discharged, and emptied in the same operational pattern already enacted by cosmos and earth.

context_deltas.mechanism: The paired record scenes generate unlike outputs. One written judgment becomes countable, opens easily, and permits return; the other becomes an unmeasured vocal totalization, 'ruin.' The focus cry is thus the dark counterpart of a manageable account, not merely an isolated emotion.

activation_trace.role: The spoken call supplies the second scene's output in contrast to the first scene's calculation.
Total loss supplies the speaker's non-numerical summary of his record.
A written fixing that imposes judgment makes the handed record causally productive rather than informational only.
Counting and accounting provide the measured outcome against which the focus's absolute cry is heard.
Opening and ease after difficulty make one record traversable.
Departure and return complete the successful record pathway that the ruin cry fails to reach.

structural_cues: The two recipients are introduced by parallel book-giving clauses, and 84:8 and 84:11 both begin their consequence with the same future sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the explicit syntactic parallel and branches for judgment, counting, ease, and return; I infer that the cry occupies the same outcome slot as the easy account. The alternative is simply two emotional consequences with no account-versus-cry contrast.

changed_reading.before: The cry is an unstructured reaction after receiving the record.
changed_reading.after: The cry is the failed side's anti-account: one word of total loss where no manageable reckoning or return remains.

context_deltas.mechanism: A record enrolls identity and fixes judgment while arriving behind the back, where concealment is turned outward. Because the focus calling root also supports claiming a right or affiliation, the ruin cry can be the collapse of a claimant's position: a counterclaim that instantly becomes a self-verdict.

activation_trace.role: Claiming a right or affiliation turns the vocal act into forensic speech by a claimant.
Loss and corruption become the verdict that replaces the failed claim.
Entering a name into a register fixes the speaker's institutional identity before he speaks.
Concealment behind backs supplies the hidden position from which the record is forced into consequence.
Turning a matter back-to-belly supplies the reversal that exposes and overturns the claimant's case.

structural_cues: 84:10 places the record behind the back immediately before the speech act in 84:11.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an identity-fixing record, concealment, reversal, and the focus branch of making a claim; I infer a forensic counterclaim that collapses into self-condemnation. The live alternative is a non-forensic lament caused by the record.

changed_reading.before: He calls only for destruction after seeing bad news.
changed_reading.after: His last claim to standing is overturned by the record, and his own mouth voices the ruin that replaces it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next root inventory holds both prayer-like calling and encounter with fire. That double image makes the focus cry an anti-prayer with a reversed answer: he calls for ruin as cessation, but what follows is continued contact with an ignited blaze.

activation_trace.role: Calling that draws an object near supplies the request side of the response structure.
Restraint and blocking make the requested object a plea that the process be stopped.
Persistence supplies the cruel inversion in which the requested ending continues.
Prayer, blessing, and mercy activate a response register around the preceding call.
Meeting fire and its heat supplies the actual response that replaces the requested cessation.
Ignition makes the response an ongoing process rather than an instantaneous disappearance.

structural_cues: 84:12 follows the call without an intervening scene and supplies the event that occurs next.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency and a next-ayah root spanning prayer and fire-contact; I infer a request-and-reversed-answer relation. The text does not grammatically label 84:12 an answer, so ordinary consequence remains live.

changed_reading.before: He calls for perdition and then separately enters fire.
changed_reading.after: He asks for a terminating ruin, but the sequence answers his anti-prayer with sustained encounter instead of release.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later explanation supplies a prior supposition that return would not occur, while the return root also contains reviewing speech. The focus call can therefore be heard as a forced recantation: the person who claimed no return now revises that claim by naming his own loss.

activation_trace.role: Claiming a right or affiliation broadens the call into a previously maintained position now under pressure.
Loss gives the forced revision its new conclusion.
Supposition and misapprehension supply the earlier proposition that reality overturns.
Return and diminution supply both the event denied and the loss encountered on returning.
Reviewing speech makes the cry function as involuntary verbal revision.

structural_cues: 84:14 retrospectively states the belief that precedes the bad record and its cry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a false supposition, actual return, and a speech-review branch; I infer that the cry performs recantation. A live alternative is that the explanation concerns conduct while the cry remains affective only.

changed_reading.before: The cry expresses pain without propositional content.
changed_reading.after: The cry is the speaker's forced retraction of 'I will not return,' with ruin replacing his former certainty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context repeatedly supplies hidden, covered, and inwardly contained material, then gives the same containing root an image of raised clamor. The focus call becomes an involuntary vent: what was concealed as inner orientation is forced through the mouth as the single word of ruin.

activation_trace.role: Vocal drawing-near provides the audible outlet through which the interior becomes public.
Opening supplies the release event that converts containment into utterance.
Hiding something in the interior supplies the person's previously sealed inward state.
Covering adds an active layer of concealment over that interior.
Holding meaning within the heart identifies what the context says is stored rather than absent.
Raised voice and clamor supply the conversion from inward containment to audible overflow.

structural_cues: The focus gives direct speech, while 84:23 later identifies inwardly stored material as already known.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, heart-containment, and clamor; I infer that the focus cry externalizes the stored interior. The alternative is that the cry only requests an outcome and does not disclose character.

changed_reading.before: The call is a new reaction produced only at judgment.
changed_reading.after: The call is the audible rupture of an interior long covered and contained, with ruin revealing what had been stored.

context_deltas.mechanism: Night gathers, the moon reaches ordered completion, and the addressee rides stacked states, including an image of closure that prevents opening out. These cues turn the focus's restraint-persistence tension into a temporal mechanism: the cry demands interruption of a sequence that keeps carrying the speaker into another enclosing state.

activation_trace.role: Turns of time that draw events place the call inside an advancing temporal process.
Restraint and blocking make the called-for object an exit or interruption.
Persistence explains why the requested interruption remains unavailable.
Gathering dispersed things starts the context's accumulation mechanism.
Completion and ordered fullness turn accumulation into a reached state rather than random motion.
One thing mounted over another gives the future transit a stacked structure.
State after state supplies the sequence whose continuation provokes the focus cry.
Closure or adhesion that prevents expansion gives each successive state a no-exit quality.

structural_cues: 84:19 repeats the same state noun and marks compelled future transit, while 84:11 already carries future modality.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies gathering, completion, stacked transit, closure, and focus persistence; I infer that the later oath describes the temporal architecture feared in the cry. It may instead describe humanity generally without specifying this speaker's experience.

changed_reading.before: He asks for one instantaneous catastrophe.
changed_reading.after: He asks for the stacked sequence to break, because each completed state carries him into another enclosing state.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing contrast explicitly negates a branch image of cutting an extension until it ceases. Against that, the focus noun's persistence branch makes the cry a demand for the cut itself. Continuity is not intrinsically reward or punishment; its value depends on what is being continued.

activation_trace.role: Blocking and turning away supply the requested interruption.
Persistence makes duration, not only destruction, the pressure inside the cry.
Negation and exception supply the operator that reverses the following cut-image.
Cutting and diminishing until extension ceases supplies the temporal endpoint explicitly negated in the contrasting outcome.

structural_cues: The final ayah closes the two-outcome structure with a negated cessation term, while the focus cry asks for an end.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a negated cut in the rewarded outcome and persistence in the focus noun; I infer a contrast in which the focus speaker longs for the cut. The text does not directly state that his punishment is uncut, so this remains exploratory rather than a duration claim.

changed_reading.before: The noun asks only for ontological destruction.
changed_reading.after: The noun also asks for duration to be cut, in contrast with an opposite outcome whose uncut continuation is desirable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant split mapping rather than the ordinary calling root. It remains anchored to word 2 and gains directional support from the immediate fire encounter; render it only as a secondary kinetic overlay, not as a replacement morphology or lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The packet maps the calling occurrence at word 2 not only to vocal calling but also to a split-root branch of forceful driving.

activation_trace.role: Rough thrusting overlays the active caller with simultaneous forced motion toward an imposed destination.
Ruin names what the driven speaker voices while being moved.
Encounter with fire supplies the destination toward which the kinetic overlay points.

changed_reading.before: The subject is only an active caller standing before his fate.
changed_reading.after: At the same moment he calls, a split-root echo lets him be heard as forcefully driven toward the fate he names.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The dairy-remnant image is materially remote and does not establish literal causation. It remains worth carrying because it is a branch of the focus verb and the fire follows immediately; downstream prose should mark it as an analogy in which a small retained remainder draws what comes after it.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Word 2 carries a branch image of a remnant left specifically to draw the remainder after it.

activation_trace.role: A retained remnant that draws more after it makes the cry a small causal residue pulling the next event into sequence.
Ruin is the content concentrated in the residue-like cry.
Ignition supplies the larger event that the preceding verbal remainder appears to draw after itself.

changed_reading.before: The cry merely precedes the fire.
changed_reading.after: The cry can be imaged as a concentrated remainder that draws the ensuing blaze after it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading is surprising because later refusals are allowed to reverse-illuminate the earlier cry, and the amen branch is peripheral to the surface form. It remains anchored in the focus's directed call and the explicit refusal of abasement; render it as structural irony, not as an assertion that the words are synonyms.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus is a directed plea voiced by the same negatively characterized group whose later scene withholds believing and bodily abasement.

activation_trace.role: A call seeking response supplies an involuntary supplicatory posture in the voice.
The request to be stopped or turned away gives that supplication its desperate object.
A response-seeking amen activates the irony of a request voiced only after belief has been refused.
Lowering and abasement supply the bodily posture refused there but echoed vocally by the ruin plea.

changed_reading.before: The cry and the refusal to prostrate are unrelated reactions.
changed_reading.after: The one who withheld bodily submission is made to perform a dark vocal analogue of it by begging for cessation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This spatialization is strange because hollow ground and a delivery-place are distant branches of the ruin noun. It remains anchored to word 3 and is materially activated by earth casting out its contents and emptying; render it as a wish-image of recontainment after exposure, never as the noun's primary lexical sense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The ruin noun at word 3 includes both a hollow and a place where something is deposited or delivered.

activation_trace.role: A hollow or depression spatializes the called-for ruin as a receiving cavity.
A place of depositing or delivery makes that cavity a desired site of re-placement.
Casting contents outward supplies the prior exposure from which the speaker seeks reversal.
An emptied place leaves no former container available, intensifying the wish for a new hollow.

changed_reading.after: After the earth ejects and exposes what it held, he can be heard wishing for a hollow that will receive and hide him again.

strongest_changes: The paired record scenes turn the cry into an anti-account: total loss replaces manageable reckoning and return.
The immediate fire ayah converts the call into an anti-prayer answered by continued encounter rather than cessation.
The denied return and speech-review branch make the cry a forced recantation of the speaker's former confidence.
Cosmic splitting and emptying let the ruin noun describe unsealing and discharge, while later layered transit makes it a plea to interrupt persistence.
Hidden and contained interior material becoming clamor recasts the cry as disclosure, not only request.
summary.what_was_special: The focus is only a short future call, yet its two root inventories cross voice, claim, collapse, restraint, persistence, hollows, and opening. Context does not collapse these into one gloss: it turns them into coexisting legal, liturgical, temporal, material, and revelatory mechanisms, while the non-dominant split root preserves a contained voice-plus-driving overlay.
remaining_uncertainties: The accusative ruin noun can remain a quoted cry, a requested object, or a compressed self-verdict; the trace preserves all three functions.
The reversed-answer relation with 84:12 is strongly sequential but is still reader-supplied rather than grammatically marked.
The temporal contrast with the uncut reward does not by itself establish the duration of the other outcome.
Material branches such as residue, hollow, and deposition are diagnostic analogies and should not displace the dominant ruin sense.
